model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route): NI to common shareholders less CET1 retention, net debt zero, per ADS (1 ADS = 1 common share), KRW flows converted to USD

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case revenue path average (years 1-10); equity CAGR rejected (see warning)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (3.8% 3yr, 6.8% 5yr) diverges by more than 30% from EPS CAGR (~12%). Causes: KRW 3.9tn of buybacks FY23-FY25 plus rising payouts under the Value-Up framework, ~KRW 1.9tn of hybrid securities redeemed net, and AOCI swings on the FVOCI bond book and IFRS 17 insurance finance reserves. FY2020 is a rate trough that flatters the 5yr EPS CAGR. None is used directly as a forward rate.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs null: bank OCF/FCF is not meaningful. SBC is ~0.8% of revenue and stable, so the SBC adjustment does not distort growth.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-single-digit growth, credit costs normalising modestly, ROTE ~11% against a 10% KRW cost of equity, everything above ~13.5% CET1 distributed. Value slightly above tangible book.
scenario_narratives.bull: Structurally higher fee and trading income plus RoRWA discipline take ROTE toward the 13% medium-term target; Korea-discount narrowing sustained by Value-Up payouts.
scenario_narratives.bear: Household-debt/PF credit cycle, NIM compression and recurring policy levies push ROTE to ~9-10%; value below tangible book.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A Korean bank is worth its tangible common equity plus the present value of returns earned above the cost of equity. KB earns ~11% ROTE against a ~10% KRW cost of equity, so fair value is close to 1.0-1.1x tangible book; the market price (~1.07x local P/TBV) already discounts the base case. Upside requires ROTE moving durably toward 13%.
key_risks_to_valuation: Korean household-debt and real-estate PF credit cycle (provisions back to FY2023's 3.1tn would cut NI by ~0.8tn)
BOK easing compressing NIM on a mostly floating-rate book
Brokerage/FVTPL gains in H1-2026 at records; reversion lowers TTM-based earnings
Recurring government-directed compensation and support programs acting as a levy
KRW/USD translation for ADR holders (USD value moves ~1:1 with the won)
Leadership change: EGM 2026-11-20 to appoint Jae Keun Lee as executive director

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (NYSE KB ADS); 52-week range 77.44-133.29. Local 105560.KS and KRW=X from the same API for the parity check.
data_sources.financials: KB_Metrics.csv / KB.duckdb (FY2015-FY2025, 20-F); 20-F FY2025 statements and capital adequacy note; H1-2026 half-year report 6-K (SEC accession 0001193125-26-350220) and preliminary results 6-Ks (Q1: 0001193125-26-171722; Q2: 0001193125-26-313193); share count from 6-Ks 0001193125-26-313200/-313202/-313206.

sanity_check_note: FALSE TRIP - denomination artefact in scripts/sanity_check.py, not a valuation problem. inputs.fx_rate is KRW->USD (dcf_engine convention); sanity_check.py reads it as quote->reporting, so the historical table multiplies the USD ADR price by 0.000745 (FY2025 'price' 0.064) and divides by KRW EPS/BVPS, giving P/E and P/B of 0.0x; the implied multiples divide the USD IV by KRW per-share figures (P/E 0.0086x). Both sides wrong by different factors, so trip_reasons are meaningless (memory: sanity-check-fx-rate-direction-conflict; same as IBN/CM/GGB). ADS ratio is 1:1, so no ADS-ratio error is layered on top. Manual recheck on one consistent basis (KRW per share, 105560.KS December closes, EPS and equity/shares from KB_Metrics.csv): FY2016-FY2025 P/E 4.6-8.8x (avg 6.4x), P/B 0.37-0.84x (avg 0.54x; book includes hybrids, so true common P/B slightly higher). Implied at weighted IV KRW 177,294/share (US$132.06): P/E 10.3x on TTM NI-to-common/share ~KRW 17,160 (< 2x avg = 12.8x), P/B 1.10x on Jun-26 common BVPS KRW 161,450 (< 1.5x max = 1.25x), P/TBV 1.13x. Neither rule breached: a genuine pass, but a NARROW one, and the IV sits above every historical year-end P/B. The market itself (local 167,400 = 1.04x P/B) already trades above the 10yr max after the Value-Up re-rating; the valuation assumes that re-rating holds (ROTE ~11% vs 10% CoE), whereas the 2016-2023 market priced KB at an implied CoE of ~15-20%. No driver change made.

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted common shares = ADS-equivalents (1 NYSE ADS = 1 common share; 20-F FY2025 cover page: 'American Depositary Shares, each representing one share of Common Stock'). 351,106,111 shares outstanding at 2026-07-23 (Q2 dividend declaration 6-K, 0001193125-26-313200; 354,687,734 issued less 3,581,623 treasury shares held for cancellation on 2026-12-23) + ~3.4m dilutive stock grants (FY2025 diluted EPS 15,261 vs basic 15,410 = 0.98% dilution) = 354.5m. Held FLAT: share-based pay is expensed inside the flow; buybacks (KRW 700bn trust running 2026-07-24 to 2026-12-16) are distributions OUT of the year-1 flow and are not pre-deducted from the count.
inputs.ads_parity_check: 2026-10-02: 105560.KS KRW 167,400 / KRW=X 1,342.51 = US$124.69 per share vs NYSE KB ADS close (current_price at price_as_of): ADR at ~0.65% discount to local, confirming 1:1. A 1:2 ratio would imply US$249.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 share-based payment expense 153,882 (KB_Metrics.csv StockBasedComp, 20-F FY2025); H1-2026 split not disclosed in the 6-K so FY2025 is used as the TTM figure. Most KB awards are cash-settled (mileage stock, long-term share-based payments) and sit inside G&A. Bank: last_fcf = TTM NI to common shareholders (parent NI 6,282,059 less hybrid-security distributions ~190,000); reported_fcf = last_fcf + SBC.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 treasury-share acquisitions KRW 1,480bn (cash-flow statement). 2026: 3,899,988 shares bought Feb-Apr (cancelled 2026-05-15, together with 14,262,733 legacy treasury shares), 3,581,623 bought Apr-Jul (cancel 2026-12-23), KRW 700bn trust Jul-Dec. Quarterly DPS KRW 1,155 (Q2 2026). Management frames ~KRW 3.7tn total 2026 shareholder return under the CET1-above-13.0-13.5% framework.
inputs.fx_note: fx_rate converts KRW (model) to USD (quote): 1/1,342.51 = 0.00074487, Yahoo Finance KRW=X at 2026-10-02T21:18Z (52-week range 1,322-1,588; 20-F convenience rate at 2025-12-31 was ~1,444.5). Per-share values are per ADS = per common share, so intrinsic_value is USD per KB ADS and directly comparable to current_price; the *_krw twins are KRW per share and comparable to 105560.KS. Parity check in ads_parity_check.
inputs.tangible_equity_note: 2026-06-30: equity attributable to parent 60,890,838 - hybrid securities 4,206,721 - intangible assets (incl. goodwill) 1,595,329 = 55,088,788; / 351.1m outstanding = KRW 156,901 per share. P/TBV at the local price ~1.07x.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Single KRW cost of equity 10.0% across all scenarios, built in the flows' own currency: Korea 10-year KTB ~3.0-3.3% + beta ~1.0-1.1 x ~5.5-6.0% equity risk premium (mature ~4.3% plus a Korea country/governance premium) = ~9.3-10.0%, rounded up for household-debt and policy-levy risk. Below the INR banks (12.5%) by the rate differential; slightly below HSBC's USD 10.5% because KRW risk-free is ~1pp lower than UST. Risk is charged once, through the bear path and weights.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: the bank flow is after all operating costs including IFRS-16 depreciation and interest; no lease adjustment.
inputs.nci_treatment: Inside the flow. 'ebitda' = PBT + SBC - pre-tax equivalent of (hybrid-security distributions ~190,000 + NCI 38,931) at 29%, so the flow is NI to COMMON shareholders. Hybrid securities (KRW 4.2tn, classified as equity, AT1) are therefore NOT also deducted in a bridge: their cost is the distribution charged in the flow.
inputs.notes: MODEL: bank -> dcf-methods routing row 'Bank, non-bank deposit taker'. Run as FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine with net_debt = 0, the house precedent for banks (HSBC, HDB, IBN, WFC, USB, TFC, NAB.AX); economically the same as residual income on tangible book (value = TCE + PV of returns above CoE). Deposits (KRW 486tn), borrowings (78tn) and debentures (80tn) are operating funding; their interest is in the flow. Reported OCF swings -9.0tn to +9.4tn and is meaningless. Engine mapping: revenue = operating income before provisions and G&A (= Metrics.csv Revenue; FY2025 17,945,162 = pre-PCL profit 10,880,589 + G&A 7,064,573). TTM to 2026-06-30 = FY25 17,945,162 - H1-25 9,091,968 + H1-26 10,107,529 = 18,960,723. PBT TTM 8,897,297 (8,183,146 - 4,649,747 + 5,363,898); tax TTM 2,576,307 = 29.0%. 'ebitda' = 8,897,297 + 153,882 - 322,438 = 8,728,741 (46.0%). FY0 check: (8,728,741 - 153,882) x 0.71 = 6,088,150 vs NI to common 6,092,059. D&A = 0 (inside G&A). 'capex' = CET1 retention holding CET1/revenue at 2.679 (13.74% x RWA 369,750bn / TTM revenue) as revenue (proxy for RWA) grows: 267.9 x g/(1+g). CET1 13.74% sits only 0.24pp above the 13.5% top of management's return threshold and that excess is already being distributed through the July buyback, so NO excess-capital credit in the bridge. TTM flatters on two counts that the base path unwinds partially: H1-26 FVTPL gains (2.59tn) and KB Securities brokerage at records, and provisions at 10.9% of revenue vs 13-19% in FY23-FY25. H2-25 carried ELS/LTV penalty provisions (Q4-25 NI only 711bn). Sources: 20-F FY2025 (KB_20F_FY2025.txt, statements at lines 87134-87290, capital adequacy 89645-89654), Q1-26 6-K (KB_6K_Q1-FY2026.txt), and the H1-2026 half-year report 6-K (0001193125-26-350220, 2026-08-14) and Q2 preliminary results 6-K (0001193125-26-313193), read directly from SEC EDGAR because they are not yet in research/KB/Extracted or core_metrics (CSV stops at Q1 FY2026 NI). DATA GAP: H1-2026 hybrid distributions and SBC not separately disclosed; FY2025-based estimates used.

interim_h1_2026.source: KB half-year report 6-K 2026-08-14 and Q2 preliminary results 6-K 2026-07-23

bear.narrative: Korean household/real-estate PF credit cycle turns: provisions return to FY2023 levels (~17-19% of revenue), BOK cuts compress NIM, brokerage income halves from records and policy levies (livelihood-finance support, ELS-type compensation, higher education tax) recur. ROTE settles near 9-10%, at or below CoE, so value sits below tangible book.

base.capex_rationale: CET1 retention = 267.9 x g/(1+g) percent of revenue (CET1/revenue 2.679 held constant, CET1 ratio held at ~13.7%).
base.growth_rationale: Year 1 (Jul-26 to Jun-27) 3.5%: loan growth ~4% under DSR/LTV curbs and RoRWA rebalancing, NIM drifting lower as BOK eases, brokerage/trading normalising from H1-26 records. Then 4-4.5% (nominal GDP plus non-bank cross-sell), fading to 2.5% nominal in perpetuity given Korea's demographics.
base.margin_rationale: TTM 46.0%. Year 1 45.5% gives NI to common ~KRW 6.3tn (~11.3% ROTE), in line with management's 'above 11%' FY26 floor rather than the 14% H1 annualised run-rate. Fades to 44.5% as provisions normalise from 10.9% toward ~12-13% of revenue and FVTPL gains revert; terminal ROTE ~11%, just above the 10% CoE.
base.narrative: KB keeps doing what it has done since 2023: mid-single-digit revenue growth, low-teens credit costs, ~11% ROTE and payout of everything above a ~13.5% CET1. Value lands slightly above tangible book, because returns only modestly exceed the cost of equity.

bull.narrative: Non-interest income is structurally higher (Korean capital-markets re-rating, KB Securities/wealth share gains), RoRWA rebalancing lifts returns on capital and credit costs stay near today's benign level. ROTE climbs toward the ~13% medium-term target; Value-Up keeps payouts high.

entry_price.hurdle_note: 15% is applied to KRW flows. KRW has no persistent inflation differential vs USD comparable to INR, so a 15% KRW IRR is roughly a 14-15% USD IRR, before FX volatility.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 13x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the house 15% to 25% because the TTM sits at a favourable point on two cyclical axes at once: provisions at 10.9% of revenue (vs 13-19% FY23-FY25) and record brokerage/FVTPL gains, while Korean household debt-to-GDP is among the world's highest and policy-directed levies recur. Bull cut to 25% (vs 35%) because KB already trades above tangible book after a ~60% re-rating off the 52-week low. Same 25/50/25 as HSBC and HDB.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.

diagnosis.detail: Structural risks in the qualitative analysis that a standard WACC may not price: cyclicality, regulatory single point of failure
